messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 Paging: cont-batch-prod (us-west-2) p99 token latency 2.3x SLO for last 5m. Auto-escalation -> #eng-oncall. Trace IDs: 7f3a, 9c1b.
Sam (oncall): on it, pulling dashboards now. anyone seeing customer reports?
Chloe (PM): got 2 inbound from an enterprise customer saying streaming responses stalled and timed out. Notifying CSM.
Maya (SRE): I see a sharp uptick in cont-batch tail at ~16:12 UTC. p95 up 40%, p99 spikes hitting 4s, normally 900ms.
Kevin (Eng-runtime): uploading some JVM/driver logs, but initial suspicion: batch packing is forming very large batches because of QC'ed long sequence requests interleaved with short ones -> padding amplification. Also KV cache churns rising.
Sam (oncall): TL;DR: mixed sequence lengths + aggressive pack window = tail amplification. need quick mitigation to restore SLOs.
Maya (SRE): reproducing on staging with similar traffic pattern (mix of 1-10 token and 800-1200 token requests) - pack window of 30ms causes streaming flush waits.
Sam (oncall): mitigation options: 1) reduce pack window to 10ms 2) enable seqlen-aware preemptive-shed to prioritize short seqs 3) route streaming traffic to dedicated low-latency pool (if capacity). Which is fastest?
Kevin (Eng-runtime): fastest is config flip for pack window and the preemptive-shed toggle. Routing needs infra approval and will take ~10-15m.
Maya (SRE): agreed. I'll flip pack_window_ms from 30 -> 8 on us-west-2 cont-batch deployment. Doing a rolling config change to avoid mass evictions.
Sam (oncall): please post exact command you use, will monitor.
Maya (SRE): running: 
```
# k8s rollout of configmap
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/cont-batch-worker PACK_WINDOW_MS=8 --record
kubectl -n inference rollout status deploy/cont-batch-worker
```
Maya (SRE): applied to canary pods, observing latency on canary -> p99 reduced from 4.2s -> 1.1s for canary traffic.
Chloe (PM): customers asking if we have ETA for full mitigation? tell them we're rolling a config change, should see improvement within 10m.
Sam (oncall): initiating canary->gradual rollout. ops-bot, mark this incident as "mitigated->in-progress" and notify CSMs.
ops-bot: Incident status updated: mitigated->in-progress. Notifying CSMs and recording timeline.
Kevin (Eng-runtime): follow-up: we need a medium-term change - seqlen-aware scheduler that weights short requests and avoids packing long ones with short ones. I can prototype, but needs perf validation.
Maya (SRE): also seeing KV eviction spikes correlated with batch size growth. We should throttle KV[caches] or increase mem cap temporarily to avoid disk paging.
Sam (oncall): action items while rollout finishes:
- Maya: finish global rollout of pack_window_ms=8 and enable preemptive_shed=true for streaming routes (command below).
- Kevin: start a PR for seqlen-aware scheduling, include perf test plan.
- Chloe: draft customer update (ETA 10m, root cause under investigation).
- Sam: monitor p95/p99, token throughput, and KV eviction metrics.
Maya (SRE): running second command: 
```
# feature flag flip
curl -X POST "https://ops-api/api/flags/contbatch/preemptive_shed" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" -d '{"value":true}'
```
Maya (SRE): global rollout started. Rolling at 5% increments every 60s.
Sam (oncall): p99 across cluster at 16:22 UTC -> dropped from 4.2s to 1.2s. p95 now back within SLO. Good sign.
Chloe (PM): CSMs updated, customers acknowledged improvement. No data loss, streaming reconnects handled gracefully.
Kevin (Eng-runtime): note: we saw a goose-egg of heavy long-hitter requests from a single tenant causing pack fragmentation. Recommend temporary tenant throttling for that customer until seqlen-scheduling lands.
Sam (oncall): assigning tenant throttling to infra-runbook. Who has the tenant mapping?
Chloe (PM): I have mapping, will coordinate with CSM to throttle by 20% for next 2 hours.
Maya (SRE): final state after full rollout (16:30 UTC): p99 stabilized ~1.0s, p95 within target. KV eviction rates down 70%.
Sam (oncall): moving to post-incident: collect flamegraphs, request/response traces, and replay traffic to validate pack heuristics. Kevin, add perf regression alerts for seqlen mix.
Kevin (Eng-runtime): will add an evaluation harness and a nightly test that simulates mixed seqlen traffic. PR will include telemetry: batch size distribution, pack wait histogram, seqlen percentiles.
Sam (oncall): owners and postmortem timeline:
- Owner (mitigation): Maya (SRE)
- Owner (root cause & fix): Kevin (Eng-runtime)
- Communication: Chloe (PM)
- Postmortem draft expected EOD tomorrow.
Sam (oncall): closing slack loop for live mitigation. If anything regresses, re-open thread or page by replying with `!page cont-batch p99`.
ops-bot: Incident resolved (mitigation applied). Please file postmortem template: /ops/incidents/new
Kevin (Eng-runtime): quick note for postmortem: consider adding sequence-length token to routing keys so packer can avoid mixing. This may require schema change in request metadata.
Chloe (PM): noted. I'll add customer impact summary and timelines for CSMs.
Sam (oncall): thanks team. Leaving follow-up tickets: #TICKET-4567 (seqlen-scheduler), #TICKET-4568 (tenant throttling automation), #TICKET-4569 (batching telemetry). Closing thread unless anyone objects. :thumbsup:
